resources.title: The water cycle around Mayon
resources.summary: A 45-minute lesson that follows rain from Mayon's slopes to the Yawa River and back to the clouds, with a cup-and-cover demonstration.
resources.subject: Science

competency.text: Describe the water cycle and how it affects the local community

requirements: One printed worksheet per pair (2 pages)
Clear cup, warm water and plastic cover for the demonstration

references.label: Team-written fictional sample for the CherIt demonstration. No external sources reproduced.

version.note: Shortened the worksheet to two pages and added a no-projector option.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

lesson.objective: Learners describe evaporation, condensation and precipitation using places they know around Mayon.

sections.heading: Materials
items: Clear cup with warm water
Plastic cover and an ice cube
Printed pair worksheet
Chalkboard sketch of Mayon, the Yawa River and Albay Gulf

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Ask: where does the rain on the school roof go afterwards? (5 min)
Cup demonstration: cover warm water, put ice on top and watch droplets form (10 min)
Trace the cycle on the board sketch: river to sky, clouds over Mayon, rain on the slopes (15 min)
Pairs label the worksheet diagram with the three stages (10 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Exit question: name one place in our barangay where you saw evaporation this week (5 min)

resources.title: The water cycle around Mayon, Bikol vocabulary version
resources.summary: Ma'am Lira's water cycle lesson with a Bikol–English word bank and a picture-matching warm-up for learners still building English vocabulary.
resources.subject: Science

competency.text: Describe the water cycle and how it affects the local community

requirements: One printed word bank per pair (1 page)
Clear cup, warm water and plastic cover for the demonstration

references.label: Adapted from “The water cycle around Mayon” version 2.0 by Ma'am Lira. Fictional sample for the CherIt demonstration.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

resources.changeNote: Added a Bikol–English word bank and a picture-matching warm-up. Removed the pair worksheet to save printing.

lesson.objective: Learners describe evaporation, condensation and precipitation, first in Bikol and then in English.

sections.heading: Materials
items: Clear cup with warm water
Plastic cover and an ice cube
Printed Bikol–English word bank
Picture cards: sun, cloud, rain, river

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Warm-up: match picture cards to Bikol words, then to English words (10 min)
Cup demonstration from the original lesson (10 min)
Trace the cycle on the board sketch, naming each stage in both languages (15 min)
Pairs explain one stage to each other using the word bank (5 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Exit question: name one stage of the water cycle in Bikol and in English (5 min)

resources.title: States of matter in the kitchen
resources.summary: Learners sort kitchen items into solid, liquid and gas, then watch ice and steam change state using a kettle.
resources.subject: Science

competency.text: Classify materials as solid, liquid or gas

requirements: Activity cards, one set per group (can be handwritten)
Kettle or thermos of hot water, handled by the teacher

references.label: Team-written fictional sample for the CherIt demonstration. No external sources reproduced.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

lesson.objective: Learners classify common kitchen materials as solid, liquid or gas and describe one change of state.

sections.heading: Materials
items: Activity cards: rice, cooking oil, salt, steam, vinegar, ice
Kettle or thermos (teacher only)
Three sorting areas on the board

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Groups sort the cards into solid, liquid and gas (10 min)
Teacher shows ice melting and steam rising (10 min)
Groups explain one card they argued about (15 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Each learner writes one solid, one liquid and one gas found at home

resources.title: Percent at the palengke
resources.summary: Learners compute discounts and mark-ups from a mock market stall, using prices written on the board.
resources.subject: Mathematics

competency.text: Solve problems involving percent, discount and mark-up

requirements: Price list written on the board

references.label: Team-written fictional sample for the CherIt demonstration. No external sources reproduced.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

lesson.objective: Learners compute a 10%, 20% and 25% discount and explain which stall offers the better price.

sections.heading: Materials
items: Board price list: fish, rice, pili nuts, abaca bag
One-page worksheet
Optional printed price flashcards

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Review: 10% of 250 by moving the decimal point (5 min)
Two stalls, two discounts: which is cheaper? (15 min)
Pairs solve three mark-up problems from the worksheet (15 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Exit slip: compute the sale price of a ₱180 item at 25% off

resources.title: Reading typhoon signals
resources.summary: Learners connect wind signal numbers to what families in a coastal barangay should prepare, using a printed signal chart.
resources.subject: Science

competency.text: Explain weather warnings and the safety measures they call for

requirements: One printed signal chart per group

references.label: Team-written fictional sample. Check current official warning definitions before teaching.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

lesson.objective: Learners match each wind signal level to a family preparation step.

sections.heading: Materials
items: Printed signal chart (groups)
Go-bag picture cards
Optional poster template

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Share: what did your family do during the last typhoon? (10 min)
Groups match signal levels to preparation cards (15 min)
Groups present one level and its steps (15 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Learners list three go-bag items and when the family should pack them

resources.title: Retelling a short Bicol-inspired story
resources.summary: Learners read a team-written short story about a fisher's daughter in Catanduanes and retell it in order using picture cues.
resources.subject: English

competency.text: Retell a story in sequence using beginning, middle and end

requirements: One story sheet per learner (1 page)
Four picture cue cards (can be drawn on the board)

references.label: Story written by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a traditional folk tale.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

lesson.objective: Learners retell the story in the right order using first, next, then and finally.

sections.heading: Materials
items: One-page story sheet
Four picture cue cards

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Read the story aloud, then together (10 min)
Order the picture cards on the board (10 min)
Pairs retell the story using the four sequence words (15 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Each learner draws and labels the story's ending

resources.title: Fractions with bibingka slices
resources.summary: Paper bibingka circles help learners compare halves, thirds and fourths before writing them as fractions.
resources.subject: Mathematics

references.label: Team-written fictional sample for the CherIt demonstration. No external sources reproduced.

permission.notice: Fictional sample created by the CherIt team for this demonstration. Not a real teacher's file.

lesson.objective: Learners fold paper circles into halves, thirds and fourths and order the unit fractions by size.

sections.heading: Materials
items: Three paper circles per learner
Worksheet
Crayons

sections.heading: Procedure
items: Fold one circle into halves and name each part (10 min)
Fold thirds and fourths; compare the slices (15 min)
Order 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 on the worksheet (10 min)

sections.heading: Assessment
items: Which slice is bigger, 1/3 or 1/4? Learners explain using their circles

seedReviews.text: The cup demonstration worked without a projector.
Two pages is easier to print. I added a short Bikol vocabulary list.
Four-page worksheet was too much to print.
Good sorting game; the steam part needs a safety note.
Learners liked the pili nut prices.
